title: In Light of Us
description: Mz.Icar Collective is an interdisciplinary group of artists creating bold, community-centered public art that blends storytelling, material culture, and speculative imagination. Their collaborative practice spans murals, sculptural installations, textiles, projection mapping, and immersive environments that invite audiences into experiences of joy, reflection, and belonging. Rooted in deep engagement with local communities and cultural histories, their work amplifies underrepresented voices while exploring how emerging technologies like augmented reality and interactive projection can support cultural storytelling and memory-making. Their projects have been installed across cities including Boston, Brooklyn, Cincinnati, Green Bay, and Philadelphia, and have been featured in collaborations with festivals and institutions such as BLINK and The Roots Picnic.

Rooted in a belief that art should bring people together, their work fosters creativity, equality, wonder, and shared moments of discovery in public spaces.

title: L1ght Graff1t1 Make0vers
description: 0H10M1ke is a Brooklyn-based interdisciplinary artist known as “The One-Line Master,” recognized for creating more than 15,000 live portraits and light-based performances across cities including New York, Miami, Tokyo, Kyoto, and Berlin. Working at the intersection of drawing, performance, and light, he translates real-time gesture into luminous forms using a Wacom tablet and stylus, treating each mark as an immediate, unrepeatable response to the moment. His ongoing series L1ght Graff1t1 Make0vers transforms participants into vivid, reimagined identities through live digital light performance, blending street aesthetics, improvisation, and spectacle. Across international exhibitions at venues such as the Park Avenue Armory, the Guggenheim Museum, and the Museum of Graffiti, his work explores light as both medium and metaphor for connection, impermanence, and shared human presence.

title: String Theory for Dummies 2.0
description: Daniel Shields is a Kentucky-based installation artist currently living outside of Cincinnati, Ohio who has used soft yarn to create immersive pieces that cover or enclose large outdoor areas since 2014, but who has only taken art seriously since 2019. Typically, his creations are, at their core, public art which manipulates innate perception of well-known locations in largely unconscious ways by segmenting and dividing 3D space with simple, sparse lines. Most installations use fluorescent acrylic yarn with UV light and UV lasers to create vibrant effects that trick the senses. Some woven installations are visitor-created, where yarn balls are provided and anyone can add their own elements, creating a truly democratic experience where signs read “please touch the art.” Like people and the relationships between them, yarn is seemingly fragile but can be stretched thin and made to endure a tremendous amount of stress without breaking – but there is a limit to everything, and strength in numbers.

Through painting and mixed-media experimentation across surfaces such as canvas, aluminum composite, and plexiglass, they distort and reconfigure imagery to create vibrant visual worlds where color drives movement, emotion, and form.

title: muon : bloom
description: Christo Squier is a composer, installation artist, and creative director whose work explores the intersection of music, science, and immersive experience. Drawing on fields such as particle physics and cognitive science, he creates generative environments that investigate perception, energy, and the boundaries between the tangible and intangible. His practice blends electronic and classical composition with installation, performance, and interactive systems, and he has collaborated with companies including Punchdrunk, Secret Cinema, and Les Enfants Terribles. He has also received commissions from Science Gallery London and Britten Pears Arts, along with awards for innovation in immersive sound. Thomas Blackburn is a creative code and audiovisual specialist with over 20 years of experience designing and programming complex audiovisual systems for performance and installation. His work spans technical production, visual art, and custom instrument design, supporting large-scale immersive projects. He has collaborated with artists including Aphex Twin, Grace Jones, Amon Tobin, and institutions such as Tate Modern and FOLD, focusing on pushing the boundaries of audiovisual performance through technology.

description: Drew Merritt is an American painter and muralist known for his striking realism and his ability to merge classical aesthetics with contemporary urban environments. Alongside his mural practice, he maintains a fine art studio practice in oil painting, exhibiting work in galleries worldwide and bridging the worlds of street art, fine art, and cultural storytelling.

title: Mural by Dulk
description: Spanish artist Antonio Segura, Dulk, is one of the most important names in Spanish painting of the moment internationally. His body of work begins to form in urban art and mural painting to which he remains closely linked today along with study work, but does not stop there. He continues to research and constantly create new forms of expression through different media, drawing, sculpture or photography among others. Dulk’s paintings are the immediate byproduct of his travels into remote areas and his memories of a natural wonder and wildlife. He has witnessed first hand both the beauty of these landscapes and the terrible collapse that is creeping over them like a fatal tide. By painting something beautiful he asks audiences to gather the strength to look away from art and toward nature, as painful as that may be. With a strong ecological conviction to defend ecosystems and the most vulnerable species, his work invites the viewer to be part of a unique imaginarium, full of energy and with a special sensitivity to color. A dream world with animals and natural spaces that tells personal, universal and unique stories.

title: Mural by Jim Tucker and Frank Young
description: Frank D. Young Frank D. Young is an American fine art photographer whose portraits treat their subjects as living documents of their existence. Though he has always had a camera in his hands, he began his journey as an artist in 2008, building a practice rooted in analog processes and equipment while moving fluidly between film and digital capture. Since 2012, he has documented the Black residents of Cincinnati's Over-the-Rhine, a neighborhood reshaped by economic revitalization and gentrification, creating a portrait record of a community in the midst of change. His clients include the Cincinnati Regional Chamber, the World Affairs Council of America, 1001 Colors, Duke Energy, Mortar, 3CDC, and The City Flea. Drawing on influences from Gordon Parks and Richard Avedon to Carrie Mae Weems, Jamel Shabazz, and Spike Lee, his work bridges documentary tradition and fine art portraiture, framing everyday people with the dignity and permanence of the historical record. Jim Tucker Jim Tucker is a British-born artist and educator whose passion is to use art to build community through collaboration and education. Since leaving England in 2007, he traveled extensively before settling in Cincinnati in 2021, carrying with him a belief in "eating what the locals eat," a phrase that signifies reverence and respect for the culture of every new place. He interprets his surroundings through site-specific automatic painting, generating imagery and characters that he contrasts with work inspired by historical and contemporary photography of the area. Since moving to Cincinnati, he has produced and painted over twenty murals, many in partnership with 1001 Colors and now recognized as city landmarks, and collaborated with institutions including the Cincinnati Art Museum, the Marketer Collaborative, and several Big Tech companies. Across a combined career of more than twenty years, his work bridges fine art, murals, and community building. The Collaboration Jim and Frank have been working together for several years, with Jim licensing Frank's photographs as references in his paintings and installations. BLINK 2026 marks the first time the two are coming together for a unique hybrid mural, combining a wheat paste of Frank's photography against Jim's painted interpretation of the mural's location.
